name: St John's wort
short: Induces drug-metabolising enzymes and lowers levels or effect of many medicines (e.g. warfarin, cyclosporin, digoxin, oral contraceptives). Serotonin syndrome reported with SSRI antidepressants.
text: Reviews describe St John's wort as having an encouraging safety profile when taken on its own, but a high potential for drug interactions. A systematic review of published literature and spontaneous case reports identified clinically significant interactions with warfarin, phenprocoumon, cyclosporin, HIV protease inhibitors, theophylline, digoxin and oral contraceptives, with a decrease in the concentration or effect of those medicines, probably through induction of cytochrome P450 enzymes and the transport protein P-glycoprotein; one such interaction with cyclosporine caused acute rejection in two heart transplant patients. Combined with serotonin reuptake inhibitor antidepressants (such as sertraline, paroxetine or nefazodone) or buspirone, it can cause serotonin syndrome, and a possible interaction with triptan migraine medicines was also identified.
